did_you_know.text: Did you know? Job chapter 26 is Job’s reply to Bildad, and it opens with the words, “Then Job answered and said.”
Did you know? Job asks sarcastically what benefit Bildad’s words have brought to someone without strength, and what deliverance has been achieved for one whose arm is powerless.
Did you know? Job also questions the wisdom of Bildad’s advice and the extent of understanding his words have provided—not merely their practical usefulness.
Did you know? Job describes the Rephaim and their inhabitants as being beneath the waters, pointing to a hidden realm associated with the world of the dead.
Did you know? According to Job, Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD; they have no covering or place hidden from his sight.
Did you know? The verse presents a picture of the earth hanging on “nothing” and the north stretched out over “emptiness”—a poetic description of the LORD’s rule over the vastness of creation.
Did you know? Job describes the LORD as gathering or holding the waters in his clouds, so that the cloud does not burst under their weight.
Did you know? This verse describes the LORD as covering or enclosing the face of his throne and spreading his cloud over it, an image expressing his majesty and the concealment of his presence.
Did you know? Job describes the LORD as marking out a circular boundary on the surface of the waters, at the point where light meets darkness.
Did you know? Even the “pillars of heaven” are described as trembling and being astonished at the LORD’s rebuke, emphasizing his power over the cosmic order.
Did you know? The LORD is described as calming the sea by his power and crushing Rahab, a figure or symbol associated with the power of the sea and chaos in biblical poetry.
Did you know? Job credits the LORD with adorning the heavens and piercing the fleeing serpent, an image of a threatening or chaotic power.

Did you know? Job concludes that all these descriptions of the LORD’s greatness are only “the outer fringe of his ways” and a faint whisper of what is heard about him; no one can comprehend the full thunder of his power.
